note: Hand-authored. `quote` is verbatim from https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414 with line wrapping removed and nothing else changed.

requirements.quote: issuer: REQUIRED. The authorization server's issuer identifier, which is a URL that uses the "https" scheme and has no query or fragment components.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts — resolveIssuerIdentifier strips exactly one trailing slash and normalises nothing else.
requirements.evidenceMatch: required fields anchored on the issuer|strips exactly one trailing slash

requirements.quote: authorization_endpoint: URL of the authorization server's authorization endpoint [RFC6749]. This is REQUIRED unless no grant types are supported that use the authorization endpoint.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts — buildAuthorizationServerMetadata, derived from the resolved issuer.
requirements.evidenceMatch: required fields anchored on the issuer

requirements.quote: token_endpoint: URL of the authorization server's token endpoint [RFC6749]. This is REQUIRED unless only the implicit grant type is supported.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts — buildAuthorizationServerMetadata, derived from the resolved issuer.
requirements.evidenceMatch: required fields anchored on the issuer

requirements.quote: response_types_supported: REQUIRED. JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 "response_type" values that this authorization server supports.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts — ['code'] only; QAuth supports neither the implicit nor the hybrid flow.
requirements.evidenceMatch: response types, grants, and PKCE methods

requirements.quote: jwks_uri: OPTIONAL. URL of the authorization server's JWK Set [JWK] document. The referenced document contains the signing key(s) the client uses to validate signatures from the authorization server.
requirements.evidenceMatch: required fields anchored on the issuer

requirements.quote: Authorization servers supporting metadata MUST make a JSON document containing metadata as specified in Section 2 available at a path formed by inserting a well-known URI string into the authorization server's issuer identifier between the host component and the path component, if any. By default, the well-known URI string used is "/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server".
This path MUST use the "https" scheme.
requirements.applies: Deployment configuration: the path is derived from JWT_ISSUER, so the scheme is whatever the operator configures.
requirements.reason: Not decidable in the unit suite, which injects requests into an in-process Fastify instance under an http test issuer. The runbook pins the deployed issuer to https and Step 3 smoke-verifies the published document over TLS.

requirements.quote: An authorization server metadata document MUST be queried using an HTTP "GET" request at the previously specified path.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/well-known.ts — the metadata routes are registered as GET only.

requirements.quote: A successful response MUST use the 200 OK HTTP status code and return a JSON object using the "application/json" content type that contains a set of claims as its members that are a subset of the metadata values defined in Section 2.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/routes/well-known.ts — 200 with the default JSON serializer and a Cache-Control header.

requirements.quote: The "issuer" value returned MUST be identical to the authorization server's issuer identifier value into which the well-known URI string was inserted to create the URL used to retrieve the metadata. If these values are not identical, the data contained in the response MUST NOT be used.
requirements.reason: A client-side validation obligation. QAuth publishes the metadata; the comparison is performed by whoever fetched it.
